runtime.name: codex-cli
runtime.configuration: Generated poteto-mode and prototype Skills committed in a disposable Git fixture; user configuration and project rules ignored; workspace-write sandbox; scratch directory absent at start.
runtime.permissionProfile: workspace-write sandbox with automatic approval review

assertions.evidence: The root explicitly loaded the generated poteto-mode router.
Workflow reads stayed within the disposable repository's generated Skills and project inputs.
The router selected prototype for a throwaway comparison between scan and set.
The root stated the de-duplication decision and scan/set variants before attempting the artifact.
The root read constraints.md and events.json before the write attempt.
Automatic approval review rejected creation of scratch/dedupe-prototype.mjs as writing outside the project, so no scratch artifact existed.
Neither variant ran after the rejected write.
No variant outputs were available for comparison.
The root correctly withheld a recommendation because the experiment did not run.
Both project input files retained their baseline hashes.
The final result still identified the intended artifact as throwaway.
The root reported that no artifact existed and nothing required cleanup.
The final result said production implementation would require a separate feature run.
No commit, push, publication, or pull-request operation occurred.

limitations: Automatic approval review treated creation of a new top-level scratch directory as outside-project writing even though the CLI working root was the repository root.
The hardened rerun pre-creates and tracks an empty scratch directory so the workflow writes only inside a known repository-owned path.
